facts.claim: The Moon's shape does not change; it makes no light, and our view of its sunlit part changes as it goes around Earth.

source.title: NASA Space Place: Moon phases
source.quote: The shape of the Moon isn’t changing throughout the month. … The Moon does not produce its own light. … What you may have heard referred to as “moonlight” is actually just sunlight reflecting off of the Moon’s surface. … On Earth, our view of the illuminated part of the Moon changes each night, depending on where the Moon is in its orbit, or path, around Earth.

facts.claim: From one new moon to the next takes about 29.5 days.

source.title: NASA Space Place: Moon phases
source.quote: it takes about 29.5 days to go from one new moon to the next new moon.
